summary: Suggests an experimental protocol that lets a host send a short message to be shown to a user on another host. Hosts may experiment with it. It was replaced by RFC 1312.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 1159 describes an experimental way to send a short message to a user on a specified host and terminal. It defines both TCP and UDP services and a compact message format.

questions: send a message to a user on another host
how do i send a message to a user on another host
what does the message send protocol do
subtitle: An experimental protocol for sending a short message to a user on another host.

tldr.problem: Some hosts did not run TCP/IP at all times but could use a simple protocol to send a short message to a user on another host.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines TCP and UDP message-send services on port 18 and a four-part message format shorter than 512 octets.
tldr.outcome: RFC 1159 is an experimental protocol and was obsoleted by RFC 1312.

today: RFC 1159 is Experimental and was obsoleted by RFC 1312.

sections.title: Purpose of Message Send
sections.content:
The Message Send Protocol sends a short message to a given user on a given terminal on a given host. The RFC compares it with the Unix write command, which is limited to users on the same host.

The memo says some hosts did not run TCP/IP at all times and might be able to use a simpler protocol implemented in a subset of TCP/IP. It also notes that SMTP already had a SEND command, but says TCP required substantial code for the intended use.
sections.plainLanguage: The protocol sends a short message to a named user and terminal on another host. It was proposed for systems that could use a simpler service than a full TCP connection.

sections.title: TCP and UDP Services
sections.content:
The TCP service listens on TCP port 18. A client establishes a connection and sends the message; data received by the client is discarded, and the client closes the connection after sending.

The UDP service listens on UDP port 18. When the server receives a datagram, it sends an answering datagram containing exactly the same data back to the client.
sections.plainLanguage: The TCP and UDP versions both use port 18. The TCP client sends over a connection, while the UDP server echoes the received datagram back.

sections.title: Message Fields and Length
sections.content:
The message has four parts: a one-octet protocol revision, the target user name, the terminal name, and the message text. The current revision value is decimal 65, the character A. The user name and remaining parts are null-terminated eight-bit characters, and the eighth bit must not be stripped.

The total message length, including all four parts and terminating nulls, must be less than 512 octets. An empty terminal part selects the appropriate terminal; an empty user part sends the message to the console.
sections.plainLanguage: The message identifies its revision, user, terminal, and text. Its total length must be under 512 octets, including the null terminators.
